chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Al-Hakam ibn Salim, who said:

A group of people came in, so he advised them, then he said: 'There is not one of you except that he has visually perceived Paradise and what is in it, and visually perceived the Fire and what is in it, if you are affirming the Book.'

key_terms.عَايَنَ: To see visually or perceive directly

ai.seo_question: How does belief in the Quran allow one to perceive Paradise and Hellfire?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam emphasizes that sincere belief in the Quran entails an internal, spiritual visualization of Paradise and Hellfire, transforming abstract doctrine into vivid mental reality. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ta'wil* (interpretive understanding) where scriptural descriptions are not merely literal promises but immediate cognitive experiences for the believer. It underscores the power of the Quran to make the unseen (*ghayb*) palpable through the faculty of faith.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Al hakam Bin Salim who said,

‘A group came over, so he<sup>asws</sup> advised them, then said: ‘There is not one of you except that he has visualised the Paradise and whatever is in it, and visualised the Fire and whatever there is in it, if you are ratifying by the Book’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim ibn Mehzam from Hakam ibn Salim who has said the following: “

Once a people came to the Imam (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah, recipient of divine supreme covenant) who granted them good advice and then said, ‘If you really affirm the Holy book there is no one among you who have not observed paradise and all that it contains or the fire with all that is in it.’”
